L25: ### What is Kv9?

L41: ### How are you assessing efficacy?
L42: 
L43: Efficacy is evaluated using gross tumour measurements of the widest diameter (industry standard) for 2 years after completing the treatment course.
L44: 
L45: ### What animals are you accepting into the trial?
L46: 
L47: We are currently accepting dogs and cats into the clinical study. Horses can enrol if they are based in the Hawkes Bay region.
L48: ### What is Kv9 regulatory status?
L49: 
L50: Kv9 is investigational and available only through approved clinical studies. The Kv9 clinical study has a Research Approval Certificate A012161-02 from MPI according to ACVM 81 Veterinary Medicine Trial Approval criteria. And ethical approval granted by Bioeconomy Science Institute (AgResearch) AEC 2026-2521-AE -13328 (2521).
L51: ### Is there a risk to an administrator if they are pregnant?
L52: 
L53: We do not anticipate there to be a risk to the administrator that use this product while pregnant, however it has not tested. If you are concerned, please contact a KVS team member to be removed from the treatment team.
L54: 
L55: ### Do you require a definitive diagnosis?
L56: 
L57: No, a suspected diagnosis from a veterinary pathologist report is sufficient. We understand that it can be difficult to obtain a definitive diagnosis for many tumour types by FNA.
L58: ### Is there a minimum or maximum dog size?
L59: 
L60: No, the treatment is dependent on the tumour size, please see our eligibility criteria for specifics.
L61: 
L62: ### How long is your enrolment open for?
L63: 
L64: We do not have a set date to close enrolment. If you would like to stay up to date on our progress, please contact our team to get place on our newsletter list.
L65: 
L66: ### How long does each treatment appointment take?
L67: 
L68: We advise to allow 20-30 minutes for treatment appointments and 10-15 minutes for monitoring appointments.
L69: ### Do I need to repeat blood work if it was done over a month ago?
L70: 
L71: Yes, we need an up to date biochemistry and CBC panel, we will work with your team to organise this if your patient is eligible for the trial.
L72: ### My patient has been put on steroids, can they enrol in the trial?
L73: 
L74: It depends. If the treatment is short term we will recommend to delay starting the trial until they have stopped taking steroids . If the treatment is long term we would recommend to taper the dose off before entering the trial. There may be a few exceptions for very low doses that are unlikely to suppress the immune system. Please contact our team if you would like to discuss the eligibility of your patient.
L75: ### What costs are covered?
L76: 
L77: KVS will reimburse the clinic for the cost of any visits required as part of the Kv9 trial. Materials required for treatment or monitoring visits will be provided by KVS. Additional visits, medications or tests are at the discretion of KVS if they are covered as part of the trial. If you are uncertain please contact the KVS team.
L78: ### My patient had surgery on their tumour, can they still participate?
L79: 
L80: It depends. There needs to be at least 1cm x 1cm of tumour to receive the treatment. So if there is tissue remaining or if it has regrown after surgery they are still considered eligible for the trial.
L81: 
L82: ### Can my patient be withdrawn?
L83: 
L84: Yes, participation is voluntary, and they can withdraw their pet from the trial at any time without penalty.
